title: Autism mutations rewire protein interaction networks to drive neurodevelopmental pathology.
data_url: https://github.com/MattStateLab/asdppi (code + one 1,879-row interaction table); PRIDE PXD047896 (raw mass spectrometry, CC0); GEO GSE285270 and GSE285273

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and opened data/ppi100.RData from the authors' GitHub: 1,879 rows, 2 columns (bait, prey gene symbols), 100 baits, 1,074 unique partners, median 11 partners per bait, 0 duplicate rows, 0 missing cells. Downloaded and parsed the PRIDE sample sheet (SampleInformation_2026.xlsx, 1,047 runs: 103 wild-type bait conditions, 106 mutant conditions, mostly 3 replicates each) and listed all 1,013 PRIDE files (98+ raw .raw files plus processed-search archives of 0.33-9.6 GB each, licence CC0). Listed the whole GitHub repository (85 files) and opened the one other large table, geneAnnotation_hek293T_ASD_DD_SCZ.csv (19,392 gene rows x 26 binary annotation columns). Read the full published article text (17-page PDF from the authors' mirror).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All interaction confidence scores, the AlphaFold-Multimer screen results (113 high-confidence direct interactions out of 1,881 pairs screened), and the mutant-versus-wild-type differential interaction table (54 patient-derived missense variants; 136 lost interactions across 95 partners; thresholds |log2 fold change| >= 1, false discovery rate < 0.1, p < 0.05) are described in the text only. Those tables are Science supplementary tables S1-S8, which returned HTTP 403 (blocked) to both the fetch helper and the web-page reader; bioRxiv supplementary files returned HTTP 429 (rate limited) on every attempt.

a1_downloadable.note: Raw mass spectrometry is public in PRIDE PXD047896 under CC0, the organoid sequencing is public in GEO, and the code repository downloads freely; no login or access application anywhere. But the processed interaction tables (supplementary tables S1-S8) were not retrievable: science.org returned HTTP 403 to every request I made.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The only downloadable processed table is a positives-only edge list (bait, prey) with no score, no p-value and no non-interacting pairs, so a label column does not exist. The interesting label - does this patient mutation weaken or strengthen this specific partnership - is not in any file I could open; it would have to be rebuilt by re-running statistics on 6.6-9.6 GB of search-engine output, or lifted from a publisher supplement I could not download.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are gene symbols only (no protein sequences, no UniProt accessions), but 1,174 symbols map to UniProt in one bulk query, so this is a minor cost rather than a killer.

a4_units_stated.note: The downloadable edge list carries no measured quantity at all, so there are no units. The quantities that have units (log2 fold change of partner intensity, false discovery rate) are only in the unavailable supplementary tables.

a5_enough_rows.note: The wild-type network has 1,879 positive pairs (verified) but zero negatives. For the mutation-rewiring task the paper reports 54 variants and 136 significantly lost interactions, i.e. a few hundred labelled variant-partner pairs at most - under the ~1,500-row bar, and I could not verify even that count.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 9.6 GB (txt_ASD_WT.zip) + 6.6 GB (txt_ASD_Mutant.zip) of search-engine output, verified from the PRIDE file listing
a6_fits_laptop.note: The route that would supply the quantitative label means downloading and re-processing two multi-gigabyte archives of peptide-level tables, which breaks both the 50 MB download rule and the ~5 GB working-set limit. The 1,879-row edge list itself is 7.5 kB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Mostly matches: the file's 1,074 unique partners and median of 11 partners per bait match the paper exactly; the row count is 1,879 against the paper's stated 1,881 interactions, a two-row discrepancy I cannot explain.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels trace back to a physical measurement (peptide intensities from affinity purification-mass spectrometry), not to another model's output. The edge list is a thresholded statistical call on those measurements, which is acceptable; the AlphaFold-Multimer scores in the paper are predictions and would be features, never labels.

existing_models.name: MutPred-PPI (2025 bioRxiv preprint, code on GitHub at rosstewart/MutPred-PPI)
existing_models.score_and_split: Per the search result summary: graph attention network over AlphaFold3 complex contact graphs with protein language model embeddings; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.85 on proteins seen in training and 0.72 on unseen proteins in cross-validation. I read the search snippet, not the full paper.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The drop from 0.85 to 0.72 on unseen proteins is their own stated generalisation gap; snippet only, I did not retrieve the discussion.

existing_models.name: eSIG-Net (Nature Methods, 2026) - a sequence-based interaction language model for mutation-driven interaction change
existing_models.score_and_split: Claims to outperform existing sequence- and structure-based methods at predicting interaction-specific rewiring from sequence alone; numbers and splits not retrieved (search snippet only).

existing_models.name: mCSM-PPI2 (Nucleic Acids Research, 2019) - predicts change in binding affinity on mutation from structure
existing_models.score_and_split: Per the search summary: Pearson correlation ~0.82 in cross-validation, 0.76 (root-mean-square error 1.19 kcal/mol) on the SKEMPI 2.0 affinity dataset. Web server, not downloadable weights.

existing_models.name: Missense3D-PPI (Journal of Molecular Biology, 2023) - rule/structure-based predictor of variant impact at interfaces
existing_models.score_and_split: Web resource; performance numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) plus AlphaFold-Multimer interface features, which is what the paper itself used
backbone.hardware: Embeddings for ~1,200 proteins run on a laptop CPU in a few hours; AlphaFold-Multimer screening does not.
backbone.licence: ESM-2 is MIT-licensed; the paper's interaction data in PRIDE is CC0, but the Science supplementary tables carry the publisher's reuse terms.

integration.partner_dataset: SKEMPI 2.0 (~8,330 measured binding free energy changes on mutation), MaveDB/ProteinGym, and the Vidal-lab yeast two-hybrid edgotyping sets
integration.join_key: UniProt accession plus residue position, resolved from gene symbols
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do models trained on biophysical binding-affinity changes in purified complexes predict which partnerships a patient mutation actually loses inside a cell - the question this dataset could have answered if the differential interaction table were downloadable.

controls.positive_control: The paper's own headline result: three FOXP1 variants and one FOXP2 variant lose the FOXP4 interaction - a model must recover these.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the mutation labels within each bait protein; performance must fall to the per-bait average.
controls.external_validation: SKEMPI 2.0 binding-affinity mutations, and the paper's own neural progenitor cell replication of the HEK293T interactions.

honest_claim_h3: Any model built on what is actually downloadable here could only claim to rank protein pairs that an overexpression pull-down in one human kidney cell line already called as interacting - it could not claim anything about which partnerships a mutation disrupts, because that measurement is not in the files.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use two protein sequences and a patient's single-letter mutation to predict whether that specific protein partnership is lost.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example would be an autism-risk protein, one of its measured partners, and one patient-derived missense change; the paper covers 54 such variants over about 100 risk proteins, so a few hundred to roughly a thousand variant-partner examples - a count I could not verify because the table is not downloadable.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the partnership gets weaker, stronger or stays the same, measured as the log2 fold change in how much partner protein is pulled down with the mutant versus the wild-type bait in affinity purification followed by mass spectrometry.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Human geneticists and the autism precision-therapy groups want to know which of thousands of uncharacterised variants break a specific molecular link rather than just 'damage the protein'; even a failed model would quantify how far affinity-based predictors transfer to in-cell pull-down measurements.

more_or_better_data.why: 54 variants with a few hundred labelled partner pairs is far smaller than what MutPred-PPI and the SKEMPI 2.0-trained models use (SKEMPI 2.0 alone holds ~8,330 measured affinity changes), and it is one cell line (HEK293T) with overexpressed tagged baits.

confidence_score.why: Three biological replicates per condition (verified in the PRIDE sample sheet) would support a per-measurement noise estimate, but only if the replicate-level intensities were accessible, and they sit inside the 6.6-9.6 GB archives.

models_beatable.why: The nearest competitors are a 2026 Nature Methods language model (eSIG-Net) and a 2025 graph attention network already evaluated on held-out proteins (0.72 area under the curve on unseen proteins); both are recent and honestly split.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: our model could not see everything theirs sees, because the differential interaction measurements this project depends on are not downloadable, and the assay (in-cell pull-down enrichment) measures a different quantity from the binding free energies those models were trained on.

ml_idea: Considered: predict mutation-induced rewiring of specific protein partnerships (which partner a patient's missense variant loses or gains) from the two protein sequences plus AlphaFold-predicted interface context, using the paper's 54-variant mutant interaction map as labels. Rejected because the label table is not downloadable and is too small anyway. The fallback - predicting the wild-type interactions themselves - fails because only the 1,879 positive pairs are released, with no scores and no tested-but-negative pairs.

effort.compute_note: Embedding time estimated as ~1,174 proteins through a small ESM-2 checkpoint on CPU; the 16.2 GB working set is the measured size of the two processed-search archives in PRIDE (9.6 GB + 6.6 GB) that would be needed to rebuild the labels. Nothing was timed.

verdict_reason: Fails A2: the only downloadable processed table is a positives-only list of 1,879 bait-partner pairs with no score and no negatives, and the mutation-rewiring label that makes the paper interesting exists only in Science supplementary tables that returned HTTP 403 or inside 6.6-9.6 GB mass-spectrometry archives. Even if obtained, 54 variants and ~136 lost interactions is below the row bar (A5), the working set breaks the laptop limit (A6), and the task is already served by open, recently and honestly evaluated models (MutPred-PPI, eSIG-Net).
